newsitem.title: USA: Budget changes Medicare fees to HMOS, Med Schools.
newsitem.headline: Budget changes Medicare fees to HMOS, Med Schools.

text.p: President Clinton's fiscal 1998 budget would make several changes in the way Medicare payments are made to Health Maintenance Organizations and to medical schools.
Health Care Financing Administration head Bruce Vladick told reporters that, contrary to some earlier news reports, there would be no freeze on HMO payments.
No region would see its payments drop and there would be a $350 floor of the monthly capitation rate. That would bring up the plans now getting the lowest payments.
"There's a safety valve," he said. "No one will see rates drop down from one year to the next."
But he said there would be an attempt to eliminate the geographical inequities in the current system. This would occur by blending local and national payment formulas.
And in the year 2000, instead of paying plans 95 percent of what the estimated average fee-for-service costs would be, that would drop to 90 percent.

Moreover, the components of the managed care payments that are supposed to go to medical schools, academic medical centers and hospitals getting disproportionate share payments for treating the poor and the uninsured will no longer go to the managed care plans. Instead they would be placed in a special fund that would support medical education and care for the poor.
